newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Shell JV refinery plan in China dropped - sources.
newsitem.headline: Shell JV refinery plan in China dropped - sources.

text.p: Royal/Dutch Shell's plan to build a 160,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) joint venture refinery in China has been dropped, Chinese sources said on Friday.
Several Chinese sources, including those at major Chinese partner China Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC), said the plan has been dropped.
Sources at Shell declined to comment specifically about the status of the refinery plan.
But one source said "we are not rigid, the important thing is to make the project economically robust and to meet everybody needs."
Sources said plans for a petrochemical plant, which were included in the original plan, would still go ahead.
But the capacity of the new petrochemical plant would be expanded to 600,000 tonnes from the initial 450,000 tonnes, the Chinese sources said.

"We want to go ahead with the ethylene plant but...for now, we have planned not to go ahead with the refinery...the decision to drop the refinery was made at end 1996," said a well placed source at China Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC), the major Chinese partner.
A separate CNOOC source said China's State Planning Commission (SPC) did not grant Shell and its partners approval to go ahead with the refinery.
The refining and petrochemical complex, planned for Huizhou, in southern China's booming Guandong province, had been on the drawing board since the late 1980's.
A feasibility study was presented to Beijing in February 1994 and a decision on whether to go ahead or not had been expected by the end of 1996.
Under the original plan, Shell owned 50 percent of the project and CNOOC 20 percent. Guangdong provincial government, China Merchant Holding Co and state refiner SINOPEC each held 10 percent.
The sources said there was surplus refining capacity in China, even if utilisation rates were low, and profit margins for refiners were generally poor.
A fresh proposal for the petrochemical plant would be submitted to the SPC for approval at a later date, one source said.
